title: Sub-Quadratic Attention Scaled to 1M Tokens
hook: Researchers just proved that one million token context windows can run four times faster without accuracy loss.
context: Published via the Frontier AI Benchmark Institute, this paper resolves persistent quadratic memory bottlenecks in transformer inference.
development: By introducing adaptive sparse attention heads and sub-quadratic token pruning, memory allocation scales linearly even under heavy loads.
explanation: Architecturally, the model dynamically filters redundant token states, dedicating full attention compute only to semantically high-value activations.
implications: For production engineering teams, this unlocks real-time document search, multi-hour video understanding, and localized reasoning on consumer hardware.
limitations: However, authors emphasize that distributed latency across multi-node clusters and edge-device thermal throttling require further optimization.
takeaway: As frontier models mature, architectural compute efficiency—not raw parameter count—is becoming the real moat.
